questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Short head of biceps attached to:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Coracoid process • Biceps brachii short head takes origin from the tip of coracoid process and the long head from the supraglenoid tubercle. Insertion is into the radial tuberosity.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Biceps brachii does NOT have attachment to:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Front of humerus • Biceps brachii short head takes origin from the tip of coracoid process and the long head from the supraglenoid tubercle of scapula.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Intracapsular but extrasynovial is:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Long head of biceps brachii • Origin of long head of biceps brachii is intracapsular and extrasynovial, but enclosed by a prolongation of synovial membrane of shoulder joint.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Muscle of arm with additional supinator action:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Biceps • Biceps brachii is a flexor at elbow joint, but it is also a powerful supinator.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Muscle NOT supplied by musculocutaneous nerve:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Extensor carpi radialis longus • Musculocutaneous nerve supplies the flexor compartment of arm region. Extensor carpi radialis longus is supplied by radial nerve.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Coracobrachialis is pierced by which nerve:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Musculocutaneous • Coracobrachialis is pierced and supplied by musculocutaneous nerve

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: After surgery on right side of neck, a person could not raise his arm above head and also could not shrug the shoulder. What are the possible causes:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Damage to spinal accessory nerve, b. Paralysis of trapezius muscle • Spinal accessory nerve runs very superficial in the posterior triangle of neck and is prone to iatrogenic injury, leading to paralysis of trapezius muscle and difficulty shrugging the shoulder, as well as overhead abduction.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Nerve supply of rhomboideus major:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Dorsal scapular nerve • Rhomboid muscles and levator scapulae are supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: INCORRECT about serratus anterior:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Supplied by thoracodorsal nerve • Long thoracic nerve (of Bell) supplies serratus anterior muscle. • Serratus anterior pulls the scapula forward (protraction). It also pulls on the inferior angle of scapula to help in lateral scapular rotation, the glenoid cavity is turned to face more directly upwards as the arm is raised from the side and carried above the head against gravity.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is climber’s muscle?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Latissimus dorsi • The muscle which becomes more evident due to contraction while climbing (like trees) is latissimus dorsi and hence is the name.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following muscles have dual nerve supply EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

Pronator teres

• Pronator teres is supplied by median nerve.

Muscles Dual

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following muscle has dual nerve supply?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Flexor digitorum profundus • Hybrid (composite) muscles have more than motor nerve supply, e.g., lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus is supplied by median nerve and the medial half by ulnar nerve.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which muscle originates from tendon of other muscle?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Lumbricals • The four tendons of flexor digitorum profundus give origin to four lumbricals.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following tear earlier gave the name to the muscle as called forgotten muscle ?

options.label: C
options.text: Long head of biceps tendon tear

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Subscapularis tendon tear Subscapularis muscle is called as forgotten muscle because it was difficult to pick earlier because of limited radiological investigations.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: When a heavy object in hand is lowered, the extension at the elbow is brought about by:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Active lengthening of the flexors • When a heavy object in hand is lowered, the extension at the elbow is brought about by active relaxation (lengthening) of the flexors - biceps (antagonist). • The antagonist muscle opposes (antagonizes) the concerned movement to makes it more controlled and precise. Though it is opposing the movement but does it with partial resistance, so that the resultant movement becomes smooth. For example, biceps opposing extension at elbow partially, so that extension becomes slow and smooth, as occurs in lowering down a heavy object in hand. • Normal extension at the elbow is by active contraction (shortening) of the extensor - triceps (agonist).

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: While carrying a heavy suitcase the downward dislocation of glenohumeral joint is resisted by the following muscles EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Latissimus dorsi • The axis of pull of latissimus dorsi doesn’t cross the shoulder joint and cannot have a shunt action on the joint. • Shunt muscles are those which stabilise the corresponding joint, when they are not producing a movement at the joint. • For example while carrying a heavy suitcase the downward dislocation of glenohumeral joint is resisted by the muscles like deltoid, coracobrachialis and short head of biceps.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: C8,T1 supplies following muscles EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Extensor indicis • The muscle of the back of forearm, extensor indicis is supplied by the radial nerve branch-PIN (posterior interosseous nerve - C7, 8 fibres). • All the hand muscles like 3 and 4 lumbricals, abductor pollicis brevis, palmar interossei are supplied by C-8 and T-1 root values.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: ‘Dropped shoulder’ occurs due to paralysis of:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Trapezius • Scapula is positioned and maintained on the posterior wall of the thorax by the tone and balance of the muscles attached to it. If trapezius muscle is paralyzed. the balance is upset resulting in dropped shoulder.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Winging of scapula is due to paralysis of:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Serratus anterior > b. Trapezius > a. Rhomboids • Winging of scapula is undue prominence of medial border of scapula, especially when an attempt is made for scapular protraction, occurs due to paralysis of serratus anterior muscle. • Secondary to serratus anterior palsy, a winged scapula is also caused by trapezius and rhomboid palsy involving the accessory nerve and the dorsal scapular nerve, respectively.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A 50-year-old female has undergone mastectomy for Ca Breast. After mastectomy, patient is not able to extend, adduct and internally rotate the arm. Nerve supply to which of the following muscles is damaged? ( )
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Latissimus dorsi • Mastectomy may damage thoracodorsal nerve leading to paralysis of latissimus dorsi. The patient finds difficulty in shoulder extension, medial rotation and adduction.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Teres major muscle is supplied by:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Lower subscapular nerve • Teres major is supplied by the lower subscapular nerve, which also supplies subscapularis muscle.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The muscle that crosses both shoulder and elbow joint is:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Biceps brachii • Long head of biceps brachii takes origin from the supraglenoid tubercle of scapula, crosses the shoulder joint and subsequently elbow joint to insert into the radial tuberosity of bone radius.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Boundaries of upper triangular space include all EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Subscapularis • Subscapularis muscle is anterior relation of upper triangular space.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The accompanying artery with axillary nerve in the quadrangular space is:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Posterior circumflex humeral artery • Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery pass through quadrangular space and then wind around the surgical neck of humerus.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following structures pierce the clavipectoral fascia EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Lateral thoracic artery • Acromiothoracic (not lateral thoracic), artery passes through the clavipectoral fascia. • Clavipectoral fascia extends between the coracoid process, clavicle, and the thoracic wall and envelops the subclavius and pectoralis minor muscles. It has a costocoracoid membrane, which lies between the subclavius and pectoralis minor muscles and is pierced by the cephalic vein, the thoracoacromial artery, and the lateral pectoral nerve.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Boundaries of anatomical snuff box are all EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Extensor carpi ulnaris

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Contents of anatomical snuff box are:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Radial Artery • Anatomic snuff box is a triangular interval bounded anterolaterally by the abductor pollicis longus (and extensor pollicis brevis) and posteromedially by the tendon of the extensor pollicis longus. • It has a floor formed by the styloid process of the radius, scaphoid, trapezium and the base of first metacarpal bone. • Radial artery is the content of the fossa, whereas, cephalic vein and cutaneous branch of radial nerve lies on the roof.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Compression of a nerve within the carpal tunnel products inability to: (; )

options.label: C
options.text: Flex the distal phalanx of the thumb

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Oppose the thumb • Carpal tunnel syndrome leads to compression of median nerve, paralysing the abductor pollicis brevis, hence loss of thumb opposition. • Thumb opposition has three components: 1. Anterior abduction of thumb (abductor pollicis brevis supplied by median nerve) 2. Medial rotation of thumb (opponens pollicis supplied by median and ulnar nerve) 3. Flexion of thumb (flexor pollicis brevis supplied by median and ulnar nerve) • Paralysis of abductor pollicis brevis leads to loss of the first component of thumb opposition, plus thumb remains in adduction deformity (unopposed adductor pollicis supplied by ulnar nerve). • In this patient there is loss of anterior abduction (abductor pollicis brevis; median nerve) but lateral abduction of thumb (abductor pollicis longus supplied by posterior interosseous nerve, radial nerve) is still possible. • Adduction of thumb is carried out by the adductor pollicis (ulnar nerve). • Since the compression of median nerve is in the carpal tunnel (paralysing the distal muscles in hand) the proximal muscles of forearm are still functional. Flexion of distal phalanx (flexor pollicis longus supplied by anterior interosseous nerve, median nerve) is possible.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Action of dorsal interossei:
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Lumbricals and all interossei • 12 muscles: 4 lumbricals and 8 interossei (4 dorsal and 4 palmar) act together to achieve glass holding position: MCP (meta-carpophalangeal) flexion and IP (inter-phalangeal) extension. • Paralysis of these 12 muscles results in comparative increased activity of antagonistic (opposite) muscles, leading to Claw hand deformity: hyperextension at MCP and flexion at IP joints.

questions.topic: DAMS · Anatomy Upper Limb-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Claw hand is hyperextension at metacarpophalangeal jointand flexion at the interphalangeal(s). Which muscles have become non-functional?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Lumbricals
